extracted.intended_audience: applicants, licensees, counsel, and other parties participating in FCC proceedings (fee applicants, broadcast/cable applicants, and COALS filers)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements for filing fee-award applications, random-selection procedures, COALS electronic filings, and nondiscrimination complaints under FCC Part 1. Covers content, timing, forms, evidence, confidentiality, and adjudicative steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of application for award
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must show that the applicant has prevailed and identify the position of an agency or agencies in the proceeding that the applicant alleges was not substantially justified; or show that the demand by the agency or agencies in the proceeding was substantially in excess of, and was unreasonable when compared with, the decision in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application shall also include a declaration that the applicant is a small entity as defined in 5 U.S.C. 601 or a statement that the applicant's net worth does not exceed $2 million (if an individual) or $7 million (for all other applicants, including their affiliates). Exceptions: applicant may omit net worth statement if it attaches an IRS ruling that it qualifies under 26 U.S.C. 501(c)(3) or, for tax-exempt organizations not required to obtain an IRS ruling, a statement describing the basis for believing it qualifies; or states that it is a cooperative association as defined in 12 U.S.C. 1141j(a). The application shall state the amount of fees and expenses sought; may include any other matters applicant wishes the Commission to consider; shall be signed by applicant or authorized officer/attorney and be accompanied by a written verification under oath or penalty of perjury that information is true and correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net worth exhibit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant except a qualified tax-exempt organization or cooperative association must provide with its application a detailed exhibit showing the net worth of the applicant and any affiliates at the time the proceeding was designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit may be in any form that provides full disclosure of assets and liabilities and is sufficient to determine eligibility under the subpart; presiding officer may require additional information. Ordinarily included in the public record, but portions may be submitted under seal as 'Confidential Financial Information' with a motion describing the information and explaining why it falls within FOIA exemptions (5 U.S.C. 552(b)(1)-(9)), why public disclosure would adversely affect applicant, and why disclosure is not required in the public interest. Sealed material served on Bureau counsel but need not be served on other parties. If presiding officer finds it should not be withheld, it will be placed in the public record; requests to inspect/copy disposed of under Commission FOIA procedures (§§0.441–0.466).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of fees and expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must be accompanied by full documentation of the fees and expenses for which an award is sought, including the cost of any study, analysis, engineering report, test, project or similar matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a separate itemized statement for each professional firm or individual showing hours spent by each individual, description of specific services performed, rate at which each fee was computed, any expenses for reimbursement, total amount claimed, and total amount paid or payable by applicant or others. Presiding officer may require vouchers, receipts, or other substantiation for expenses claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing fee-award application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be filed whenever the applicant has prevailed in the proceeding or in a significant and discrete substantive portion of the proceeding, or when the demand of the Commission is substantially in excess of the decision in the proceeding, but in no case later than 30 days after the Commission's final disposition of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If review or reconsideration is sought or taken of a decision the applicant believes it prevailed on, award proceedings are stayed pending final disposition. 'Final disposition' defined as the later of: (1) date an initial decision or recommended disposition becomes administratively final; (2) issuance of an order disposing of petitions for reconsideration; (3) if no petition filed, last date on which such petition could have been filed; (4) issuance of a final order or other final resolution not subject to reconsideration or judicial review; or (5) completion of judicial action and any subsequent Commission action pursuant to judicial mandate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and service of award documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application for an award or other pleading relating to an application shall be filed and served on all parties to the proceeding in the same manner as other pleadings in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: confidential financial information may be submitted under §1.1512(b) directly to the presiding officer in a sealed envelope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer to fee-award application (Bureau counsel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after service of an application Bureau counsel may file an answer to the application; failure to file within 30 days (unless extension or statement of intent to negotiate filed) may be treated as consent to the award request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau counsel and applicant may jointly file a statement of intent to negotiate, which extends answer time by 30 days and may be further extended by presiding officer. The answer must explain in detail any objections and identify facts relied on; if based on facts not in the record, include supporting affidavits or request for further proceedings under §1.1526.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 15 days after service of an answer, the applicant may file a reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reply is based on alleged facts not in the record, the applicant must include supporting affidavits or request further proceedings under §1.1526.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments by other parties on award applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party to a proceeding other than the applicant and Bureau counsel may file comments on an application within 30 days after it is served or an answer within 15 days after it is served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commenting party may not participate further in proceedings on the application unless the presiding officer determines that the public interest requires such participation to permit full exploration of matters raised in the comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement of award claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant and Bureau counsel may agree on a proposed settlement of the award before final action on the application, either in connection with a settlement of the underlying proceeding or after it has concluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a prevailing party and Bureau counsel agree on a proposed settlement before an application has been filed, the application shall be filed with the proposed settlement. If a presiding officer (other than the Commission) approves the settlement, it shall be forwarded to the Commission for final determination. If the Commission is the presiding officer, it shall approve or deny the proposed settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further proceedings for award applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of an award will ordinarily be made on the written record, but the presiding officer may order further proceedings (informal conference, oral argument, additional written submissions or evidentiary hearing for issues other than excessive demand or substantial justification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further proceedings held only when necessary for full and fair resolution and shall be prompt. Whether the agency's position was excessive demand or substantially justified is determined on the administrative record as a whole. A request for further proceedings must specifically identify information sought or disputed issues and explain why additional proceedings are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial decision content for award applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A presiding officer shall issue an initial decision as soon as possible after completion of proceedings on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision shall include written findings and conclusions regarding eligibility, whether applicant was prevailing party or whether agency demand was substantially in excess and unreasonable compared to the adjudication, explanation of reasons for differences between amount requested and amount awarded, findings on whether Commission's position was substantially justified, whether applicant unduly protracted proceedings, committed willful violation, acted in bad faith, or whether special circumstances make an award unjust. If multiple agencies are at issue, decision shall allocate responsibility for payment and explain the allocation. When Commission is presiding officer, it may issue but is not required to issue an initial or recommended decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission review of initial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Either the applicant or Bureau counsel may seek Commission review of the initial decision in accordance with §§1.276–1.282; Commission may also review on its own initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neither party seeks review and Commission does not, the initial decision becomes final 50 days after issuance. Review is discretionary; if review taken, Commission will issue final decision or remand to presiding officer for further proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review of awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial review of final agency decisions on awards may be sought as provided in 5 U.S.C. 504(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment procedure for awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant seeking payment of an award from the Commission shall submit to the General Counsel a copy of the Commission's final decision granting the award, accompanied by a statement that the applicant will not seek review in the United States courts, or a copy of the court's order directing payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will pay the amount awarded unless judicial review of the award or the underlying decision has been sought by the applicant or any other party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of random selection procedures (Subpart L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of subpart L apply to applications for initial licenses or construction permits or for major changes in facilities of authorized stations in specified services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies where indicated in §1.1601 and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation for random selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing applications for an initial license or construction permit shall be designated for random selection and hearing in accordance with the procedures set forth in §§1.1603–1.1623 and §73.3572.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications shall be tendered, accepted or dismissed, filed, publicly noted and subject to random selection and hearing per relevant rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of random selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Random selection probabilities will be calculated in accordance with the formula set out in §§1.1621–1.1623.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-selection hearing and grant conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Following random selection, the Commission shall announce the 'tentative selectee' and, where permitted, invite Petitions to Deny its application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If after any necessary hearing the Commission determines the tentative selectee has met the requirements of §73.3591(a), it will grant; if unable to make such a determination, it shall order another random selection among remaining mutually exclusive applicants. If papers show a substantial and material question of fact, it shall designate that question for hearing; hearings conducted by a presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: medium of mass communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Medium of mass communications means: (1) a daily newspaper; (2) a cable television system; and (3) a license or construction permit for specified broadcast services (TV incl. low power/translator, AM, FM, DBS transponder under editorial control, Multipoint Distribution Service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note clarifies daily newspaper means published four or more days/week, in English, circulated generally in the community of publication; college newspapers not considered circulated generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: minority group
rubrics_metrics.description: Minority group means: (1) Blacks, (2) Hispanics, (3) American Indians, (4) Alaska Natives, (5) Asians, and (6) Pacific Islanders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: owner for preference purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner means the applicant and any individual, partnership, trust, unincorporated association, or corporation which: (1) if applicant is proprietorship, is the proprietor; (2) if partnership, holds any partnership interest; (3) if trust, is beneficiary; (4) if unincorporated association/non-stock corporation, is a member or, for nonmembership, a director; (5) if stock corporation, is beneficial owner of voting shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note 1: for diversity preference, only other ownership interests of those with 1% or more beneficial interest are cognizable. Note 3: spouse's ownership interests of an applicant's principal will not presumptively be attributed to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferences for random selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants desiring a preference must indicate it in their application and list any owner who owns all or part of a medium of mass communications or who is a member of a minority group, with precise identification of ownership interest or minority group. Applicant must state whether more than 50% of ownership interests are held by minority group members and number of media >50% owned by applicant/owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference factors: (b)(1) applicants >50% owned by members of minority groups—2:1; (b)(2) applicants whose owners in aggregate hold >50% interest in no other media—2:1; (b)(3) applicants whose owners hold >50% interest in one, two or three other media—1.5:1. Applicants may receive (b)(1) and either (b)(2) or (b)(3). Preferences determined based on ownership interests as of release of latest Public Notice. Restrictions: no preferences under (b)(2) or (b)(3) for certain LPTV or MDS applicants if owners' aggregated interests in other media wholly encompass or are encompassed by the protected predicted contour/service area (list of contour computations provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Probability calculation for random selection
rubrics_metrics.description: All calculations computed to no less than three significant digits; probabilities truncated to the number of significant digits used in a lottery and calculated via multi-step procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: (b) divide total applicants into 1.00 for pre-preference probabilities; (c) multiply each applicant's pre-preference probability by applicable preference from §1.1622(b)(2) or (b)(3); (d) divide each result by sum to determine intermediate probabilities; (e) add intermediate probabilities of applicants who received those preferences; (f) if sum ≥ .40 proceed to (g); if < .40, multiply each intermediate probability by .40/sum and divide .60 by number of applicants without those preferences to determine their new intermediate probabilities; (g) multiply each applicant's probability by preference ratio from §1.1622(b)(1); (h) divide each probability by sum to determine final selection percentage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of COALS (Subpart M)
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide electronic filing of applications, notifications, registration statements, reports, and related documents in the Multichannel Video and Cable Television Services and the Cable Television Relay Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of COALS
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart applies to filings required by §§76.403, 76.1610, 76.1801, 76.1803, & 76.1804, and 78.11 through 78.36 of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key COALS definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions include: (a) Application—request on Form 327 or similar to amend/modify/renew authorizations or assign/transfer control; (b) Authorization—written instrument issued by FCC or authority conveyed by rule upon filing; (c) COALS—the consolidated database and electronic filing system for MVCTS and CARS; (d) CARS—services authorized under part 78; (e) Filings—applications/notifications/registrations/reports in plain text or on FCC Forms 320,321,322,324,327; (f) MVCTS—services authorized under part 76; (g) Receipt date—date application received at Commission or lock box; major amendments per §78.109 result in new receipt date; (h) Signed—original hand-written signature for manual filings or electronic signature consisting of the name transmitted via COALS entered on filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Station files as official records
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, notifications, correspondence, electronic filings and other material and copies of authorizations comprising technical, legal, and administrative data relating to each system are maintained by the Commission in COALS and the Public Reference Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These files constitute the official records for these stations and supersede any other records, databases or lists from the Commission or other sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required forms and electronic/manual filing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators and applicants shall use specified forms and associated schedules: FCC Form 320 (Basic Signal Leakage Performance Report), 321 (Aeronautical Frequency Notification), 322 (Cable Community Registration), 324 (Operator, Address, and Operational Information Changes), 327 (Application for Cable Television Relay Service Station License).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Six months after the Commission announces availability for electronic filing, all filings using these forms and associated schedules must be filed electronically per COALS instructions. Electronic filing methods: batch (data transmission in single action, compiled overnight, no immediate correction) and interactive (screen-by-screen prompting with immediate prompts for out-of-range entries). Attachments should be uploaded with electronically filed applications in PDF when possible. Manual filing remains allowed with appropriate fees and addresses; manual filings requiring fees must comply with §0.401(b). Forms may be reproduced per §0.409. Applications requiring prior frequency coordination must complete coordination per §78.36 prior to filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings must contain all information requested on the applicable form and any additional information required by rules in this title and rules pertaining to the specific service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antenna locations: describe transmitting antenna site(s) by geographic coordinates specified in degrees, minutes and seconds to the nearest tenth of a second using NAD83 datum. Antenna structure registration: owners must notify FAA and register with FCC as required by Part 17; applications proposing new/existing antenna structures must contain FCC Antenna Registration Numbers or sufficient information to verify registration is not required. Environmental concerns: applicant must indicate at filing whether Commission grant may have a significant environmental effect as defined by §1.1307; if yes, file Environmental Assessment per §1.1311 and environmental review must be completed before construction. International coordination: channel assignments/usage under part 78 subject to treaties/agreements with Canada and Mexico. TINs: all filers required to provide Taxpayer Identification Numbers per DCIA; FCC may use TIN to collect and report delinquent amounts to Department of the Treasury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and correction of filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Regardless of filing method, submissions with insufficient fee, grossly deficient or inaccurate information, or without a valid signature will be dismissed immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is later found to have minimal deficiencies, the filer will be notified and allowed 15 days to correct or amend if the amendment is minor. A timely corrected application will ordinarily be processed as a minor amendment and will not affect the initial filing date or filing priority. If the amendment is not a simple correction but a major amendment, it will be treated as a new application with a new filing date and new fees. Failure to submit amended application within the specified period may result in dismissal for failure to prosecute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Subpart N (nondiscrimination on basis of disability)
rubrics_metrics.description: To effectuate section 119 of the Rehabilitation, Comprehensive Services, and Developmental Disabilities Amendments of 1978, which amended section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act to prohibit discrimination on the basis of disability in programs or activities conducted by Executive agencies or the United States Postal Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of disability nondiscrimination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Part applies to all programs or activities conducted by the Federal Communications Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs/activities of entities that are licensed or certified by the FCC are not covered by these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of auxiliary aids
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary aids means services or devices that enable persons with impaired sensory, manual, or speaking skills to have an equal opportunity to participate in and enjoy benefits of programs or activities conducted by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: for persons with impaired vision—readers, Brailled materials, audio recordings; for persons with impaired hearing—telephone handset amplifiers, telephones compatible with hearing aids, TTY/TDDs, interpreters, CART, captioning, notetakers, written materials, and similar services/devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a complete complaint (disability complaints)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete complaint means a written statement, or a complaint in audio, Braille, electronic, and/or video format, that contains the complainant's name and address and describes the Commission's alleged discriminatory action in sufficient detail to inform the Commission of the nature and date of the alleged violation of section 504.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It must be signed by the complainant or someone authorized to do so for them; printed complaints require signature; complaints in audio/Braille/electronic/video formats shall contain an affirmative identity statement functionally equivalent to a signature. Complaints filed on behalf of classes or third parties shall describe or identify (by name, if possible) the alleged victims of discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: facility (for nondiscrimination rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facility means all or any portion of buildings, structures, equipment, roads, walks, parking lots, or other real or personal property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: individual with a disability
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual with a disability means any individual who has a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, has a record of such an impairment, or is regarded as having such an impairment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical or mental impairment includes physiological disorders/conditions, cosmetic disfigurement, anatomical loss affecting body systems (neurological, musculoskeletal, special sense organs, respiratory including speech, cardiovascular, reproductive, digestive, genitourinary, hemic/lymphatic, skin, endocrine), mental or psychological disorders (e.g., intellectual disability, organic brain syndrome, emotional/mental illness, specific learning disabilities), and diseases/conditions such as cerebral palsy, epilepsy, muscular dystrophy, cancer, heart disease, diabetes, drug addiction and alcoholism. Major life activities include caring for oneself, performing manual tasks, walking, seeing, hearing, speaking, breathing, learning, and working. 'Has a record of such an impairment' means history of or misclassification. 'Is regarded as having an impairment' includes being treated by the Commission as having a limitation, being limited only as a result of attitudes of others, or having none of the impairments defined but treated as having one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: qualified individual with a disability (intro)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified individual with a disability means—
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition begins in text but is continued beyond this chunk; indicates existence of a standard to determine who is 'qualified' for programs/activities.
